definition: Diversify means to make something varied; to add variety or different kinds of elements to it.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word diversify. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know diversify should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Her financial adviser urged her to diversify, spreading her savings across stocks, bonds, and real estate instead of betting everything on a single company.
To supplement something is to add a little more of what it already has, while to diversify it is to add genuinely different kinds of elements.
To diversify something is to widen its variety, but to overhaul it is to tear the whole thing down and rebuild it from the ground up.

To vary something is to introduce changes so it is not always the same, and the changes can stay within one kind: varying the route, the pace, the seasoning. To diversify is stronger — it adds genuinely different kinds of elements, changing what the thing is made of.

To broaden something is to widen its range or reach while it stays the same kind of thing, the way a course can cover more topics. To diversify is to change the makeup itself, bringing in new and genuinely different kinds of elements.

To expand something is to make it larger — more size, more volume, more amount. Something can expand while staying entirely one kind of thing, which is why expanding is not the same as diversifying, which means adding genuinely different kinds of elements to the mix.
to make everything conform to one model
to reduce something to a smaller range

Diversify means to make something varied; to add variety or different kinds of elements to it.
After months of selling nothing but grilled cheese, Marcus decided to diversify his food truck's menu, adding tomato soup, three kinds of salads, and a rotating dessert special.
Regulars who had grown bored began returning and bringing friends.
Marcus takes a menu that was all one thing and adds several different kinds of items to it, and that act of adding variety is exactly what it means to diversify.
neutral, common in business and finance
Diversify often appears in economic contexts, as in 'diversify a portfolio' or 'diversify the local economy,' but it works anywhere variety is being added, from menus to music playlists.
Remember that it names a process, an action someone takes, so it always describes adding variety to something, not the state of already having it.

WKPR had played nothing but classic rock for thirty years, and its ratings had sunk along with its listeners' median age.
The new manager did not want a bigger tower or longer broadcast hours; reach was not the problem.
What the station needed, she argued, was to diversify.
Within a year the schedule held a morning news block, a Friday jazz hour, a call-in gardening show, and bilingual sports commentary -- kinds of programming the old WKPR had never carried.
Advertisers who had ignored the station for a decade began calling, drawn by audiences no single format could have gathered.
